controls.title: Ensure SSH root login is disabled
controls.implementation_task: Set `PermitRootLogin no` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` or a configuration file under `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/`, then reload the SSH daemon.
controls.verification_method: Run `sshd -T | grep permitrootlogin`. The output must be `permitrootlogin no`.
controls.justification: Disabling direct root logins over SSH forces administrators to authenticate with individual user accounts before using privilege escalation (for example, `sudo`). This improves accountability, provides an audit trail, and reduces the risk associated with direct root credential compromise.

controls.title: Ensure fs.suid_dumpable is configured
controls.implementation_task: Inside `/etc/sysctl.d/`, edit or create a `.conf` file and add the following line: `fs.suid_dumpable = 0`. Apply the change with `sysctl --system`.
controls.verification_method: Run `sysctl fs.suid_dumpable` and verify the value is set to `0`.
controls.justification: Core dumps may contain sensitive information such as passwords, cryptographic keys, or other confidential data stored in memory. Disabling setuid core dumps reduces the risk of credential disclosure.

controls.title: Ensure password expiration is configured
controls.implementation_task: Edit `/etc/login.defs` and configure `PASS_MAX_DAYS` with a value greater than `0` according to the local security policy. The CIS Benchmark recommends `365`.
controls.verification_method: Run `grep -Pi -- "^\h*PASS_MAX_DAYS\h+\d+\b" /etc/login.defs` and verify the value is set to `365`.
controls.justification: Limiting password lifetime reduces the window of opportunity for attackers to exploit compromised credentials. Regular password rotation decreases the impact of credential theft while remaining aligned with CIS recommendations.

controls.title: Ensure telnet client is not installed
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1021.001 (Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol/Remote Login)
controls.implementation_task: Remove Telnet clients by running `apt purge telnet inetutils-telnet`.
controls.verification_method: Run `dpkg-query -s telnet >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'telnet package is installed'` and `dpkg-query -s inetutils-telnet >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'inetutils-telnet package is installed'`. No output should be returned.
controls.justification: The Telnet protocol transmits all communications, including credentials, in clear text. SSH provides encrypted communications and should be used instead.

controls.title: Ensure events that modify /etc/group information are collected
controls.implementation_task: Create or edit a file ending with `.rules` under `/etc/audit/rules.d/` and add the rule `-w /etc/group -p wa -k identity`. Load the new rules with `augenrules --load`.
controls.verification_method: Run `auditctl -l | grep /etc/group` and `grep /etc/group /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules`. The configured audit rule must be present in both outputs.
controls.justification: Monitoring modifications to `/etc/group` helps detect unauthorized privilege changes or account manipulation attempts. Such events are valuable indicators of compromise and support forensic investigations.

controls.title: Ensure SSH MaxAuthTries is set to 3 or less
controls.implementation_task: Edit `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (or a file under `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/`) and set `MaxAuthTries 3`. Reload the SSH daemon using `systemctl reload ssh`.
controls.verification_method: Run `sshd -T | grep maxauthtries` and verify the output is `maxauthtries 3` or a lower value.
controls.justification: Limiting the number of authentication attempts reduces the effectiveness of brute-force attacks against SSH services while remaining compliant with the CIS Ubuntu Benchmark.

controls.title: Ensure password quality requirements are configured
controls.implementation_task: Install `libpam-pwquality` if required and configure `/etc/security/pwquality.conf` with at least `minlen = 14`, `minclass = 4` (or equivalent character class settings), and ensure `retry=3` is configured in `/etc/pam.d/common-password`.
controls.verification_method: Run `grep ^minlen /etc/security/pwquality.conf` and verify `minlen = 14`. Also verify `pam_pwquality.so` is referenced in `/etc/pam.d/common-password` with `retry=3`.
controls.justification: Strong password complexity requirements significantly increase the cost of password guessing and brute-force attacks while aligning with CIS Ubuntu Benchmark 22.04 recommendations.

controls.title: Ensure default user umask is 027 or more restrictive
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1083 (File and Directory Discovery)
controls.implementation_task: Configure `UMASK 027` in `/etc/login.defs` and ensure login shells inherit this value.
controls.verification_method: Run `grep ^UMASK /etc/login.defs` and verify the configured value is `027` or more restrictive.
controls.justification: A restrictive default umask prevents newly created files and directories from being unnecessarily accessible to other local users, reducing the exposure of sensitive information.

controls.title: Ensure a default deny firewall policy is configured
controls.implementation_task: Configure UFW with a default deny policy for incoming traffic using `ufw default deny incoming`, allow required services only, then enable the firewall using `ufw enable`.
controls.verification_method: Run `ufw status verbose` and verify the default policy is `deny (incoming)` and only required ports are allowed.
controls.justification: A default-deny firewall policy minimizes network exposure by ensuring only explicitly authorized services are reachable, reducing the attack surface of the server.

controls.title: Ensure unnecessary services are disabled
controls.asset_scope: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS servers running unnecessary enabled services
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter)
controls.implementation_task: Review enabled systemd services and disable services that are not required for system operation. Example: `systemctl disable --now service_name`. Services such as snapd, ModemManager, avahi, bluetooth, or unused database/web services should be removed or disabled when not required.
controls.verification_method: Run `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --state=enabled` and verify that only required services are enabled. Review services using `systemctl status service_name`.
controls.justification: Every enabled service increases the attack surface of the system. Reducing unnecessary services limits the number of exposed components that could contain vulnerabilities or be abused by attackers.

controls.title: Ensure GRUB bootloader password is configured
controls.asset_scope: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS servers using GRUB2 bootloader
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1542.003 (Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts)
controls.implementation_task: Configure authentication protection for GRUB2 by creating a GRUB administrator password using `grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2`, adding the generated password hash to `/etc/grub.d/40_custom`, then regenerate the configuration with `update-grub`.
controls.verification_method: Run `grep password /boot/grub/grub.cfg` and verify that a GRUB password configuration exists.
controls.justification: Without GRUB authentication, an attacker with physical access can modify boot parameters, bypass security controls, or boot into recovery environments with elevated privileges.

controls.title: Ensure firewall rules are configured and active
controls.asset_scope: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS servers using iptables or nftables firewall
controls.implementation_task: Configure host-based firewall rules according to server requirements. For Ubuntu systems, configure UFW or nftables rules and ensure default policies restrict unauthorized inbound traffic. Example: `ufw default deny incoming` and allow only required ports.
controls.verification_method: Run `ufw status verbose` or `iptables -L -n -v` and verify that firewall rules exist and that unnecessary inbound connections are blocked.
controls.justification: A properly configured firewall reduces exposure of network services and prevents unauthorized access attempts against vulnerable or unnecessary listening ports.

controls.title: Ensure file integrity monitoring software is installed
controls.asset_scope: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS servers containing sensitive system files
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1565.001 (Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation)
controls.implementation_task: Install and configure a file integrity monitoring solution such as AIDE. Example: `apt install aide aide-common`, initialize the database with `aideinit`, then schedule regular integrity checks.
controls.verification_method: Run `dpkg -s aide` and verify the package is installed. Run `aide --check` and verify unauthorized modifications are detected.
controls.justification: File integrity monitoring helps detect unauthorized changes to critical operating system files, binaries, and configuration files that could indicate compromise.

controls.title: Ensure system logging is configured for remote log storage
controls.asset_scope: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS servers requiring centralized logging
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1562.002 (Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging equivalent)
controls.implementation_task: Configure rsyslog to forward security logs to a centralized logging server. Edit `/etc/rsyslog.conf` or files under `/etc/rsyslog.d/` and configure remote forwarding using TCP or UDP.
controls.verification_method: Run `grep @ /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf` and verify that remote logging destinations are configured. Restart rsyslog using `systemctl restart rsyslog`.
controls.justification: Remote log storage prevents attackers from deleting local evidence after compromising a system and improves incident investigation capabilities.

controls.title: Ensure default permissions and umask are configured securely
controls.asset_scope: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS user environments and system accounts
threat_mapping: MITRE ATT&CK: T1222.001 (File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification)
controls.implementation_task: Configure a restrictive default umask value. Edit `/etc/login.defs`, `/etc/profile`, and shell configuration files to set `umask 027` or stricter according to organizational policy.
controls.verification_method: Run `grep -R "umask" /etc/login.defs /etc/profile /etc/bash.bashrc` and verify that the configured value is 027 or more restrictive.
controls.justification: A restrictive umask prevents newly created files and directories from being readable or writable by unauthorized users, reducing accidental data exposure.
